(Memphis, Tennessee) | college = *[[Hiwassee College|Hiwassee]] (2000–2001) *[[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] (2001–2004) | draft_year = 2004 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 36 | draft_team = [[Orlando Magic]] | career_start = 2004 | career_end = 2009 | career_number = 1 | career_position = [[Point guard]] | years1 = {{nbay|2004|start}}–{{nbay|2005|end}} | team1 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | years2 = 2006–2007 | team2 = [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] | years3 = 2007–2008 | team3 = [[PBC Lukoil Academic|Lukoil Academic]] | years4 = 2009 | team4 = [[Czarni Słupsk]] | highlights = * [[Conference USA Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Conference USA Player of the Year]] (2004) * First-team All-[[Conference USA]] (2004) }} '''Antonio Cornell Burks''' (born February 25, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and Europe. At {{convert|6|ft|0|in|m|abbr=on}}, he played as a guard. Burks played at [[Booker T. Washington High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Booker T. Washington High School]] in Memphis, then one year at [[Hiwassee College|Hiwassee Junior College]] in [[Madisonville, Tennessee]] before joining the [[University of Memphis]] as an invited [[Walk-on (sport term)|walk-on]]. He helped the Tigers win the [[2002 National Invitation Tournament|NIT in 2002]]. His senior year he was named the Conference USA player of the year. After a career at the University of Memphis, he was a second round draft pick of the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[2004 NBA draft]]. He was then traded to his hometown [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for cash considerations.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130115091820/http://www.cbc.ca/news/story/2006/10/02/nba-heat-burks.html|title=Burks bolts Grizzlies for Heat}} Burks averaged three points in 24 games in his rookie season. After appearing in four games for the [[Miami Heat]] during the 2006 preseason, he was signed by them on October 2, 2006.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/|title=The official site of the NBA for the latest NBA Scores, Stats & News. | NBA.com|website=www.nba.com}} but was waived on October 26, prior to the beginning of the [[2006–07 NBA season]].{{Cite web|url=http://media.www.dailyhelmsman.com/media/storage/paper875/news/2007/04/05/Sports/Old-Tigers.Still.Roaring-2824479.shtml|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090726113213/http://media.www.dailyhelmsman.com/media/storage/paper875/news/2007/04/05/Sports/Old-Tigers.Still.Roaring-2824479.shtml|url-status=dead|title=Old Tigers still roaring|archivedate=July 26, 2009}} Burks later played with [[KK Crvena zvezda]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian basketball league]]. He signed with [[PBC Lukoil Academic|Lukoil Academic]] in Bulgaria in August 2007.[http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/15167/448/item Lukoil Academic adds Antonio Burks] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071020184900/http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/15167/448/item |date=October 20, 2007 }} According to a eurobasket.com report, Burks was banned for a season from [[International Basketball Federation|FIBA]], because KK Crvena zvezda had informed them that Burks had broken the rules of his contract by leaving 20 days earlier.{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/reports/2007/11/11.asp|title=Eurobasket Daily News Report|website=www.eurobasket.com}} On July 20, 2009, Burks was shot by a robber in Memphis. Burks underwent several surgeries and recovered in the hospital.[https://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2009/jul/20/former-tiger-antonio-burks-shot-during-robbery/ Antonio Burks shot during robbery], Commercial Appeal, 20 July 2009 The man who shot him was convicted of attempted second-degree murder and other charges and was sentenced to 97 years in prison; he will become eligible for parole in 2050.[http://southmemphis.wmctv.com/news/crime/59236-man-who-shot-antonio-burks-sentenced-97-years Man Who Shot Antonio Burks Sentenced to 97 Years] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402085556/http://southmemphis.wmctv.com/news/crime/59236-man-who-shot-antonio-burks-sentenced-97-years |date=April 2, 2012 }}, Commercial Appeal, 8 September 2011 He had been released on probation for another crime only a month before shooting Burks.[http://www.myfoxmemphis.com/dpp/news/crime/darquan-swift-found-guilty-in-antonio-burks-shooting-rpt-20110701 Darquan Swift Found Guilty in Antonio Burks Shooting] {{webarchive
